options: I wish I had told you yesterday.
I hope I get to tell you tomorrow.
I wish I hadn't told you.
items.explanation: No -me, no “not”: söyleseydim = “I wish I HAD told you.” English and Turkish agree here.

options: I wish I hadn't sent this message.
I wish I'd sent this message.
I hope I get to send this message.
items.explanation: -me in Turkish — and a “not” in English too. Göndermeseydim — “I wish I hadn't sent it.”

options: I wish he had come yesterday.
items.explanation: Without -ydı it's -sA — a wish about now or later: “if only he would come.”

options: If we'd left earlier, we'd have made it.
We left early and made it.
If we leave earlier, we'll make it.
items.explanation: -sAydI = “if we had…,” -(A/I)rdI = “we would have…”. We didn't leave — we didn't make it.
-sAydI with an exclamation is a soft reproach: “you could've asked me!”

items.translation: I wish I had studied more.
items.explanation: This is the past — you need -ydı (the English “had”). In çalış the last vowel is a, so -saydım.

items.translation: I wish you had come too.
items.explanation: gel has the vowel e — so -se and -ydi. English “had” is the same for everyone, Turkish is not: you — -n, gelseydin.

items.translation: I wish we had gotten up early.
items.explanation: We — -k at the very end, not a separate word. kalk has the vowel a: kalksaydık.

items.translation: I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
items.explanation: English has “hadn't” here — so Turkish has -me: yemeseydim.

items.translation: If I'd taken an umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten wet.
items.explanation: If I had… = -sAydI, I wouldn't have… = -mAzdI. Alsaydım.

items.translation: If you'd let me know, I'd have met you.
items.explanation: You didn't let me know — I didn't meet you. A condition in the past: verseydin.

pairs.right: if I had come, I would have seen

items.explanation: -sA — now and later (“if only”). -sAydI — the past only: regret (“I wish I had”), condition (“if I had”) or reproach (“you should have!”). -me = “not.”

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence. Leave the extra forms on the plate.

items.translation: I wish I had called you yesterday.
items.explanation: Yesterday — past, -ydı. “I wish I had” has no “not,” and Turkish has no -ma: arasaydım.

items.translation: If we had left earlier, we would have made it.
items.explanation: If we had left = çıksaydık, we would have made it = yetişirdik.

items.translation: I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
items.explanation: You ate it and regret it — so “I wish I hadn't”: yemeseydim.
A reproach about the past — sorsaydın.

exercises.instruction: Receipt of regrets: pick a form for each line and tear it off.
exercises.description: The register at a pastry shop in Antalya prints lines with a blank. The learner picks one of three forms: -sA, -sAydI or -mAsAydI — with a button, keys 1–3, or a finger.

items.ru: I wish I had taken that last slice.
items.explanation: The slice is gone — past. “I wish I had” has no “not,” and neither does Turkish: alsaydım.

items.ru: I wish I had told you yesterday.
items.explanation: Yesterday — past. “I wish I had told you” = söyleseydim.

items.ru: I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
items.explanation: You ate it and regret it — Turkish adds -me: yemeseydim.

items.ru: I hope the weather's nice tomorrow.
items.explanation: Tomorrow isn't the past yet. English may step back (“I wish it would be nice”), Turkish doesn't: -sA without -ydı, olsa.

items.ru: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.
items.explanation: Unreal past: çıksaydık … yetişirdik.

items.ru: You could've asked me! I'd have known.
items.explanation: A reproach about the past — sorsaydın.
Tomorrow is the future. It takes -sA without -ydı — no stepping back in time like in English.

items.statement: “Keşke gitmeseydim” means “I wish I had gone.”
items.explanation: -me flips the meaning: gitmeseydim — “I wish I hadn't gone.”

items.translation: I wish we had studied too.
items.explanation: oku has the vowel u — so -sa and -ydı. We — -k: okusaydık.

items.prompt: “If I had had the money back then, I would have bought that house”:
items.explanation: Past condition — olsaydı, result — alırdım.
English “had” is the same for every person; Turkish is not. They — -ler: gelselerdi. -k is “we,” -niz is “you all.”
